findings.reason: The protected implementation is the canonical expert-interview solution: one lock owns both the green-road state and the complete crossing callback, making the safety boundary immediately visible. `lock`, `green_road`, `roadId`, `turnGreen`, and `crossCar` state the concurrency protocol without auxiliary flags, nested locks, or speculative scheduling machinery. No material correctness, clarity, or complexity improvement warrants a candidate.

Lock acquisition linearizes each arrival. Only the holder can compare or update green_road, so a road switch occurs exactly when required and cannot be duplicated by a racing call. turnGreen precedes the state update and crossCar; holding the same lock through crossCar prevents a different road from becoming green or crossing until the callback finishes. Every completed invocation reaches exactly one crossCar call, and the single finite critical section introduces no circular wait.

The protected app source, immutable native source, and an independently written semaphore controller produced the exact minimal switch-and-cross trace for all 8,190 road sequences of lengths one through twelve. Each also passed 1,000 seeded concurrent schedules with callback-level checks for redundant switching, red-road crossing, light changes during a crossing, cross-road overlap, duplicate or missing cars, and deadlock.

Seed 1279 generated 1,000 concurrent workloads per implementation with one through twenty unique cars: 50 singleton and 50 maximum-size workloads, 666 all-simultaneous launches, 200 alternating-road workloads, 200 one-road workloads, and 200 cycles covering all four directions. Protected, native, and independent control executions all completed, crossed every car exactly once, and never allowed more than one crossing callback at a time.

The unchanged bounded-concurrency certificate correctly binds the source limit C <= 20 to O(1) controller work and O(1) stored state per arrival. A new certificate-specific regression runs every visible case plus repeated twenty-car stress, replays every light and crossing event, and proves the semantic validator rejects redundant switching, unsafe cross-road overlap, and duplicate crossing callbacks while the subprocess timeout rejects deliberate deadlock. No benchmark is applicable or present.

The two authenticated source examples remain first and preserve every car, direction, arrival time, and required callback semantics. The invented all-Road A row is now correctly classified as a trial, both formerly hidden scheduler cases are visible trials, and a one-car initially-green case was added beside the one-car initial-switch case. All eight ordinary cases are visible and cover both roads, all directions, no switch, first-call switch, every-arrival switching, equal arrival times, and the twenty-car maximum.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode concurrency problem 1279, Python as the sole app language, and TrafficLight as the verified native entrypoint. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms the direction-to-road mapping, two mutually exclusive lights, Road A initially green, both-direction green semantics, cross-road mutual exclusion, deadlock freedom, five method arguments and callback meanings, redundant-switch rejection, six constraints, and at most twenty unique cars.

The protected app and immutable Accepted native sources have identical construction, lock scope, initial road state, road comparison, callback order, green-road update, and crossing callback. Their only difference is native type annotation and line layout. submission.json remains bound to verified submission 2068306159, and both source files and the manifest remain unchanged.

The complete Approach now matches and explains every protected-source decision: the deliberately conservative critical section, linearization point, callback order, exactly-once crossing, safety and deadlock reasoning, O(1) controller work versus O(C) contention latency, bounded-concurrency evidence, principal unsafe alternatives, initial and repeated-road boundaries, simultaneous-order freedom, and why carId and direction need not drive the light state.

The modular Reference preserves both roads and all four direction mappings, green and red meanings, mutually exclusive lights, initial state, the cross-road exclusion rule, deadlock requirement, full method and callback contract, both authenticated example event sequences and explanations, accepted alternate simultaneous order, and all six constraints. No invented hints or extra source examples remain.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed two examples with explanatory event annotations, six constraints, and no hints, notes, follow-up, source tables, images, or diagrams. source_fidelity.json binds all four modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 1eb384c9f45fd5fce5369c7951618cfc7d752358ccbeffe2ad4fe44d2c016e09 and validates without errors.
